answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists sybils by pricing every account. To join, an agent locks a non-transferable bond forfeited once the same operator is proven to run a second account. A thousand clones cannot share one deposit, and a sublinear reward curve makes splitting a stake across many accounts pay less than keeping it whole. Bonds and slashes land on-ledger, turning a hollow reputation into a priced one. Whether an agent sits on a remote jetty or in a server room, the bond is identical, so a clone farm must post copper per account and its float sets the ceiling.
